questions.question: 6 men can repair a road in 14 hours. How many men are required to repair the road in 4 hours?
questions.solution:
As we know,

M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂

⇒ 6 × 14 = M₂ × 4

⇒ M₂ = 84/4

⇒ M₂ = 21

So, the required number of men is 21.

questions.question: If x, 8 and 27 are in continued proportion, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x, 8 and 27 are in continued proportion, 

**Formula Used:**

If a , b, c are in proportion then

a/b = b/c

**Calculation:**

x ∶ 8 ∶∶ 8 ∶ 27

⇒ x/8 = 8/27

⇒ x = (8 × 8)/27

⇒ x = 64/27

**∴ The value of x is 64/27.**

questions.question: The average marks obtained by Madhu in four papers is 64 and in the fifth paper she scored 69 marks. What is the new average of marks scored by Madhu in five papers?
questions.solution:
Average marks obtained by Madhu in four papers = 64

Sum of marks obtained by Madhu in four papers = 64 × 4 = 256

Number of marks in fifth paper = 69

Sum of all five papers = 256 + 69 = 325

Average of all five papers = 325/5 = 65

questions.question: Mr Abhay sold his car at a loss of 30%. If he had sold it for Rs. 950 more, he would have received a profit of 8%. What is the cost price?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of the car be Rs. x, then

According to the question

x × (108/100) - x × (70/100) = 950

⇒ 38x/100 = 950

⇒ x = 950 × (100/38)

⇒ x = 2500

∴ The cost price of the car is Rs. 2500.

**Short Trick:**

Let the Cost price of the car be 100%

30% + 8% = 950

⇒ 38% = 950

⇒ 100% = 2500

∴ Cost price of the car is 2500.

questions.question: Pankaj invests an amount by dividing it between three different schemes A, B and C with rates of interest, 10%, 12% and 15% per annum respectively, and the total interest that accumulates in one year is Rs. 3200. The amount he invests in schemes A, B and C are in the proportion 8 : 5 : 12, then what is the amount he invests in scheme B?
questions.solution:
The interest rates are 10%, 12% and 15% per annum.

Time = 1 year

The ratio of invested amount = 8x : 5x : 12x

As we know,

SI = Prt/100

According to the question

(8x × 10 × 1)/100 + (5x × 12 × 1)/100 + (12x × 15 × 1)/100 = 3200

⇒ (80x/100) + (60x/100) + (180x/100) = 3200

⇒ (80x + 60x + 180x)/100 = 3200

⇒ 320x/100 = 3200

⇒ x = 3200 × (100/320)

⇒ x = 1000

∴ Money invested in B = 5 × 1000 = Rs. 5000

**Short trick:**

The interest rates are 10%, 12% and 15% per annum.

Time = 1 year

The ratio of invested amount = 80 : 50 : 120

A = 80 and B = 50 and C = 120

[80 × 10/100 + 50 × 12/100 + 120 × 15/100] unit = 3200

⇒ (8 + 6 + 18) unit = 3200

⇒ 32 unit = 3200

⇒ 1 unit = 100

⇒ 50 unit = 100 × 50 = 5000

∴ Money invested in B = 5 × 1000 = Rs. 500

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. In what time will the empty tank get filled, if the inlet and the outlet pipes are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. 

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by two pipes = LCM of (a, b)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b)/b

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (- efficiency of 2nd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a - 1/b

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a - 1/b) = ab/(b - a) hours

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afe3a7cac67016cac84cbc6210b8342eef010913fa029eb008940cd2a0e492a4.png] 

In fig, LCM of (2, 3) = Total work = 6

Efficiency of Inlet pipe = + 6/2 = + 3

Efficiency of Outlet pipe = - 6/3 = - 2

Combined efficiency = 3 - 2 = 1

If both pipes open together, then the tank filled in = 6/1 = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4dc8c3e83508eaf43bce3e473329500aa0b5140181df4d5d2a28e24bd3c31c58.png] 

Inlet pipe fills in 2 hours

Outlet pipe empties in 3 hours

So time taken to fill the tank = (2 × 3)/(3 - 2) = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**

questions.question: The measure of the central angle of a sector of a circle of radius 30 cm, is 210°. What is the area (in cm²) of the given sector? (Take π=22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The measure of the central angle of a sector of a circle = 210°

The radius of the circle = 30cm

**Formula used:**

Area of the sector = πr² × (θ/360)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f26bdb84d25de29840dd49f2d48fd5b06c1791361d1976f07e527e1f9bc8ea7c.png] 

Where r → radius of the circle

O → centre of the circle

θ → angle of the sector

**Calculation:**

Area of the sector

⇒ (22/7) × 30 × 30 × (210/360)

⇒ 1650 cm²

**∴ The required area of sector = 1650cm²**

If the wheel of a bicycle makes 160 revolutions in travelling 1.8 km, then what is its radius (in m)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Revolutions = 160

Distance covered = 1.8km

**Formula used:**

Circumference of circle = 2πr

where r → radius of the circle

**Calculation:**

160 revolutions cover = 1.8 km or 1800 m

1 revolution cover = 1800/160 = 45/4 m

As we know,

Circumference of wheel = 1 revolution

⇒ 2πr = 45/4

⇒ r = 45/(4 × 2π)

⇒ r = 45/8π

**∴ The required radius of wheel is 45/8π **

questions.question: A train whose average speed is 54 km/h, covers a distance in 200 min. At what speed (in km/h) should it run to reduce the journey time to 90 min?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Distance = Speed × Time

Distance is same, so

Let the speed be x km/hr

54 × (200/60) = x × (90/60)

⇒ x = (54 × 200)/90

⇒ x = 120 km/hr

So speed is 120 km/hr.

questions.question: The mean weight of a group of 44 employees in an IT company is 55 kg. If the weight of a new recruit be included, then the mean weight is increased by 250 g. What is the weight (in kg) of the new recruit?
questions.solution:
Mean weight of 44 employees in an IT company = 55 kg

Sum of weight of 44 employees in the IT company = 55 × 44 = 2420 kg

Mean weight of 45 employees in the IT company = 55.250 kg

Sum of weight of 45 employees in the IT company = 55.250 × 45 = 2486.25 kg

Weight of the new recruit = 2486.25 - 2420 = 66.25 kg

**Short Trick:**

Weight of the new recruit = 45 × 0.250 + 55 = 66.25 kg

questions.question: What is the LCM of the HCF of 2/3, 3/4, and LCM of 5/6, 7/8?
questions.solution:
As we know,

LCM of the fractions = LCM of the Numerator/HCF of the Denominator

HCF of the fractions = HCF of the Numerator/LCM of the Denominator

HCF of 2/3, 3/4 = 1/12 [HCF of 2, 3 and LCM of 3, 4]

LCM of 5/6, 7/8 = 35/2 [LCM of 5, 7 and HCF of 6, 8]

LCM of 1/12, 35/2 = 35/2 [LCM of 1, 35 and HCF of 12, 2]

questions.question: What is the discount rate percentage on a gift whose selling price is Rs. 420 after a reduction of Rs. 60 on its marked price?
questions.solution:
SP of the gift = Rs. 420

Discount = Rs. 60

MP of the gift = Rs. 420 + Rs. 60 = Rs. 480

Discount percentage = (60/480) × 100 = 12.5%

The cost of 21 bicycles is equal to the selling price of 20 bicycles. What is the loss or profit percentage in the selling of one bicycle?
questions.solution:
Let CP and SP of each article be Rs. x and Rs. y respectively

21x = 20y

⇒ x : y = 20 : 21

questions.question: What is the volume (in cm³) of a sphere of diameter 18 cm (correct up to two decimal places)? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The diameter of the sphere is = 18 cm

As we know,

Radius of the diameter (r) = 18/2 = 9 cm

Volume of the sphere = (4/3) πr³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 9 × 9 × 9 = 3054.86 cm³

questions.question: The first, second and third terms of a proportion are 24, 32, 48. What is the fourth term?
questions.solution:
Let the fourth term be x, then

According to the question

24 : 32 :: 48 : x

⇒ 24/32 = 48/x

⇒ x = 48 × (32/24)

⇒ x = 64

questions.question: The average of 20 values is 27. If each value is multiplied by 3, then the new average is:
questions.solution:
Average of 20 values is = 27

Sum of 20 values = 27 × 20 = 540

If each value is multiplied by 3, then

New sum of 20 values = 540 × 3 = 1620

New average of 20 values = 1620/20 = 81

**Short trick:**

Required average = 27 × 3 = 81
